messages:
sam_support: heads-up — customer on Dedicated reporting repeated timeouts during long streaming generations (~40-60s). They say they set a 120s deadline but the Python SDK raises a TimeoutError at ~30s. Repro snippet below, from the customer. Can someone advise? @anya_engineer

anya_engineer: can you paste the exact snippet + SDK version? streaming or non-streaming? :thinking:

sam_support: sure, here it is (redacted):
```python
from redwood import Client
client = Client(api_key=os.environ['REDWOOD_KEY'])
# customer claims they set a long timeout via env var and client arg
os.environ['REDWOOD_TIMEOUT'] = '120'  # what they did
# call they used
resp = client.generate(model='redwood-large', prompt='long story...', stream=True)
for chunk in resp:
    print(chunk.text)
# observed: SDK raises TimeoutError after ~30s with a "read timeout" message
```
They report using `redwood-sdk==0.9.1` and running on a Dedicated pool.

anya_engineer: thanks. couple quick things: 1) env var precedence and client arg behavior changed across 0.9.x -> 0.10.x; 2) streaming uses chunk-level deadlines (to avoid hanging connections) + an overall request deadline. If the env var maps to the old per-connection read timeout it can cut streams early. What exact exception text did they paste?

sam_support: message was `TimeoutError: Read timed out after 30.0s (stream chunk deadline)` — the customer copy/pasted that. They also said they set `REDWOOD_TIMEOUT=120` in their container env and also call `Client(timeout=120)` in code (they tried both).

derek_oncall: that stack matches a known bug in 0.9.1 where `REDWOOD_TIMEOUT` was wired to the socket read timeout only (per-chunk), not to the total request deadline. Fixed in 0.10.0 — PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/1234 (adds explicit `stream_chunk_timeout` + `total_timeout` separation). Workarounds: either upgrade to >=0.10.0, or set the client to pass explicit kwargs to the streaming call: `client.generate(..., stream_chunk_timeout=90, total_timeout=120)` (the streaming call kwargs override env var in 0.9.x).

sam_support: helpful — customer is on a managed Dedicated deploy and asks if we can hotfix or if they must upgrade. Any chance of a server-side mitigation?

anya_engineer: server-side can't safely change the client's socket-level timeout; we either patch SDK or give the call-level override. If they cannot upgrade immediately, tell them to call `client.generate(..., stream_chunk_timeout=90)` from their app. If they can't change code, upgrade is the only robust fix.

deploy-bot: release v0.10.0 published to PyPI at 2026-03-12T11:32:00Z (contains stream timeout separation + docs). :rocket:

support-bot: created internal ticket #7892, added follow-up to docs about env var vs client arg precedence and streaming chunk deadlines.

sam_support: forwarding workaround + recommend upgrade to the customer. will follow up with logs after they try the call-level override. :thumbsup:
